Abstract
Internet of Things (IoT) is adopted in a wide spectrum of applications in which a vast amount of data are produced 
and distributed to centralized cloud platforms to deliver various services. It involves smart devices that collect 
thousands of terabytes of heterogeneous data and deployed this to make instant decision that aids for the better 
performance and most comfort life. Traditional IoT architecture is heavily centralized, where it stores the most 
sensitive information that creates the multiple threats and security breaches as the attackers target towards these 
centralized cloud systems. To improve the security chain in IoT environment, edge computing (EC) was introduced 
to distribute the applications of IoT at the edge of the communication networks. However, these edge-based IoT 
are also vulnerable to many threats due to their decentralized and in secured management. Block chain (BC) 
technology offers a most trusted solution to resolve the security issues in the IoT-Edge computing environment. 
This research study presents the block chain driven medical image encryption technique using modified honey 
badger optimization with the ensemble chaotic systems. The proposed block chain framework uses the divergent 
methods that integrates differential scroll, Hénon chaotic maps and modified honey badger optimization to gener-
ate the optimum keys and high secured image data. These high secured data are stored in the block chain, ensur-
ing the image security to be stored in edge nodes. The complete framework was experimented using Ethereum 
using Ganache API and Python3.19 are utilized as the major programs for designing the varied interfaces of the 
recommended model. The comprehensive experimentation is undertaken to assess the security strength of the 
recommended encryption scheme. The evaluation metrics like as NACI, UACI, Entropy and standard verification 
methods such as NIST standard tests are deployed and analyzed. To prove it security strength, proposed secured 
BC framework is compared with the wide-variety of secured frameworks. The experimental findings reveal that 
the suggested framework establishes a more robust and secure environment for image exchange, surpassing the 
performance of other blockchain-based systems in terms of integrity, robustness and security. Finally, the paper 
spreads the bright light of advantages in deploying the proposed framework to formulate the most secured envi-
ronment in the IoT-Edge environment for medical image transmission.
Keywords  IoT · Edge computing · Blockchain · Modified honey badger · Scroll · Hénon maps · Ethereum

1  Introduction
Internet of Things (IoT) have seen a brighter light of growth by integrating with emerging technologies such as 
wireless sensor networks (WSN) [1], 5G/6G communication networks [2] and artificial intelligence (AI) [3]. 
Thus the combination of IoT and cloud platform is an effective solution that pushes the people’s life into their 
comfort life [4].
Sine heterogeneous data captured in IoT are usually related to the sensitive information which is to be pro-
tected against the different attacks. Privacy protection has become most prioritized concern for the people using 
IoT technology [5]. Due to the diversity of devices, the centralized cloud is often utilized as a primary solution 
within many current IoT architectures to efficiently store and manage data accessible from any location. However, 
these centralized systems are vulnerable to significant security threats [6] that could potentially compromise 
IoT infrastructure operations [7–9]. Some of the risks associated with centralized architectures include: (1) DoS 
Attacks—A successful attack on a centralized server can jeopardize data security, leading to a single point of 
failure; (2) Sensitive data stored in centralized servers lacks sufficient control over who can access it.
Edge computing assisted IoT devices can be used to perform data processing, communication and decentral-
ized storage of data on the edge of the networks which are nearer to the terminal devices [10]. The proposed 
IoT-edge model mitigates the limitations of cloud-based architecture by decreasing bandwidth usage, enhancing 
response times, and offering mobile, context-aware services. However, the integration of real-time monitoring 
and widespread applications in IoT-edge technologies has led to security vulnerabilities, complicating synchro-
nization and interoperability.
Recently, Blockchain technology has gained an eagle view on providing the more secured framework against 
the multiple attacks that causes the security breaches in IoT-Edge technology [11–13]. Blockchain relies on a 
decentralized ledger system in contrast to traditional centralized databases which the traditional IoT adopts for 
storing and sharing the data. As the security issues are resolved by these technologies, integrating block chain 
with the edges are considered to be more promising paradigm for securing the sensitive information against the 
growing attacks [14–16].
1.1  Motivation
It is important to note that block chain that the increasing demand for technological advancements is driving the 
rapid acceleration of IoT-enabled systems. These systems may also contain vulnerabilities that must be properly 
evaluated prior to adoption and implementation. Furthermore, there may be trade-offs between security and per-
formance, because blockchain technology can be computationally costly and need large resources. Motivated by 
this aforementioned problem, this research article proposes high secured framework MEDI-HONEY blockchains 
(MHBL) that combines Block chain in conjunction with ensemble chaotic encryption and modified honey badger 
algorithm for secured sharing and storing the medical images gathered by utilizing the IoT devices. MHBL offers 
an innovative solution to securely manage medical data by deploying a decentralized block chain system, thus 
offering minimal resource consumption.
1.2  Contributions

management and user revocations while maintaining the data privacy. This approach enhances the data protec-
tion, computational complexity making it deployable for the IoMT environment. The essential contribution of 
the article pursues:
1.	 The paper proposes the blockchain robust architecture for a medical image sharing that ensembles the strong 
cryptographic authentication framework for an effective data process and sharing.

2  Related Works
Ali et al. [17] introduced an encryption methodology for healthcare data that leverages a Hénon chaotic map and a 
logistic tent map. Here, the user first creates a private encryption key using the public key provided by the medical 
center. The recommended chaos-based method for encrypting medical images then employs this private key for 
encryption. Following encryption, the user digitally signs the encrypted image and forwards it to the administra-
tors. Subsequently, the healthcare organization generates a shared secret key by integrating the ciphered image, 
secret key, and digital signature. This secret key is then utilized by the authority to decrypt the image, verify it 
against an authentication factor, and confirm its validity if approved.
Khayyat et al. [18] introduced a blockchain-enabled shark smell model enhanced by chaotic networks, designed 
to secure encryption on industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) platforms. This approach integrates a combination 
of chaotic maps, specifically blending staged logistic and tent maps, to perform the initial processing of health-
care image datasets. The model is tend to improve the chaotic variables that can tend to improve the encryption 
schemes.
Hosny et al. [19] propose using fractional-order chaotic systems to encrypt color images. The 4D hyperchaotic 
Chen system of fractional order is paired with the Fibonacci Q-matrix to form the strong encryption process. The 
three-tier framework is designed for producing high randomness encrypted sequences in which confusion and 
diffusion operations are employed using 4D hyperchaotic Chen system with fractional orders. This framework 
produced the best randomness bits suitable for counterfeiting the multiple attacks.
R. Naga and Bhama [20] developed a novel blockchain-based medical image encryption framework for IoT net-
works, termed B-SCORE. The innovative tri-layered architecture incorporates image aware segmentation (IAS), 
and a blockchain environment. Experimental results demonstrated remarkable encryption performance, achiev-
ing a number of pixel change ratio (NPCR) of 99.65%, unified average changed intensity (UACI) of 33.95%, and 
entropy values approaching the ideal 8. However, this approach involves a considerable computational overhead.
Ali et al. [21] propose a blockchain-integrated data protection approach for IoT-based healthcare. This system 
leverages homomorphic encryption to protect patient data while enabling secure computations on encrypted 
information, with smart contracts managing access control. Smart contracts enforce access control and audit 
records enhance transparency. Experimental results show the model effectively protects data confidentiality, but 
challenges like communication costs and transaction volume remain.
Bhaskaran et al. [22] prescribes an innovative blockchain-integrated secure lightweight cryptography-based 
image encryption system. This system ensures image privacy on the Industrial IoT platform by providing encrypted 
pixel values through the blockchain network.

3.1.1  Honey Badger Algorithm
The honey badger algorithm (HBA) mimics the foraging trait of the honey badger, a mammal with distinctive 
black and white fur, typically found in semi-desert and rainforest environments in Africa. This algorithm is 
inspired by the honey badger’s two-phase hunting strategy. In the first phase, the badger uses its keen sense of 
smell to estimate the location of its prey. Upon arriving at the approximate location, it wander around the prey to 
find the optimal spot for digging and capturing it. In the second phase, the badger relies on the assistance of the 
honeyguide bird to locate beehives directly. The detailed description of each phase is discussed below.

3.5  Medical Image Encryption Process
To encrypt the medical images, combination of modified honey badger optimization, Hénon a scroll chaotic maps 
are employed. In this research, two-fold process is employed: 1) Optimum Key generation process 2) Encryption 
and Decryption process. The detailed description is presented as follows.
3.5.1  Optimum Key Generation Process
The MHB (modified honey badger) optimization algorithm is constructed with the application of scroll maps 
which is used to produce a vast array of distinct sequences instead of random ones, simply by modifying their 
initial values. In the key generation process, theory of scroll maps was applied to honey badger optimization to 
improve convergence speed and avoid getting stuck in local minima. This kind of integration will produce more 
repetitive chain of random numbers that aids for producing the more random sequences that can defend against 
the multiple attacks. As the first step, modified honey badger optimization models is adopted to generate the initial 
populations and deployed for generating random positions of honey badgers using chaotic variables.
After obtaining the scroll random variables, random variables are then scaled to the length of input medical 
images. (Byte Size is 256). Finally, the obtained random variables and user data are scrambled using genetic DNA 
encoding techniques to generate the optimum and high randomness keys to mitigate the attacks.

3.6  Encryption Process

3.7  Block Chain Layers
In the current study, BC technology is utilized to securely store encrypted medical images, ensuring their privacy 
and security. BC serves as a valuable ledger for maintaining data integrity and has facilitated “controlling opera-
tions” for numerous decentralized industrial devices, enabling peer-to-peer interactions across a global network 
of decentralized devices. Additionally, BC provides accountability and control across all independent systems 
while addressing security challenges. In various industrial sectors, a private BC has been employed to enhance 
security. The term “Hyperledger Fabric” refers to a BC-based framework that meets the requirements for an IoT-
Edge platform. This framework proves advantageous in several domains, including transportation, healthcare, 
extensive IoT data management, and supply chain logistics. Furthermore, BC supports decentralization, privacy, 
and trust. It also simplifies connectivity among multiple devices. The IoT-edge nodes act as nodes that initiate the 
transmission of images. These nodes exchange encrypted data with other peer nodes, ensuring that unauthorized 
entities cannot access the information.
a. Distributed ledger: this system employs a distributed ledger, a fundamental aspect of blockchain technology, 
to record data from IoT nodes in a decentralized manner, eliminating the need for a central authority or a single 
point of vulnerability. This decentralization enhances the system’s resilience against attacks and data breaches.
b. Consensus mechanisms: Blockchain relies on consensus protocols to ensure uniform agreement across the 
network regarding transaction validity and their sequence on the blockchain. Common methods include Proof-of-
Work (PoW) and Proof-of-Stake (PoS). These mechanisms guard against malicious activities by requiring network 
participants to either solve complex computational problems or stake their tokens. To safeguard sensitive data, 
the proposed research will utilize PoW.
c. Secured data: the framework can employ encryption methods to protect sensitive information, such as 
personal details, within the proposed system. Encrypted data can be stored either on the blockchain or in external 
storage systems. Only authorized edge nodes with the decryption keys will have the ability to access and utilize 
this protected information.
d. Cryptographic security: Blockchain technology incorporates cryptographic techniques to safeguard data 
and transactions. The proposed cryptographic methods ensure secure communication and authentication. They 
also enable users to verify their identities and securely sign transactions. Hash functions assign a unique identifier 
to each data piece, maintaining the integrity of the information stored on the blockchain.

Abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) is adopted in a wide spectrum of applications in which a vast amount of data are produced and distributed to centralized cloud platforms to deliver various services. It involves smart devices that collect thousands of terabytes of heterogeneous data and deployed this to make instant decision that aids for the better performance and most comfort life. Traditional IoT architecture is heavily centralized, where it stores the most sensitive information that creates the multiple threats and security breaches as the attackers target towards these centralized cloud systems. To improve the security chain in IoT environment, edge computing (EC) was introduced to distribute the applications of IoT at the edge of the communication networks. However, these edge-based IoT are also vulnerable to many threats due to their decentralized and in secured management. Block chain (BC) technology offers a most trusted solution to resolve the security issues in the IoT-Edge computing environment. This research study presents the block chain driven medical image encryption technique using modified honey badger optimization with the ensemble chaotic systems. The proposed block chain framework uses the divergent methods that integrates differential scroll, Hénon chaotic maps and modified honey badger optimization to gener- ate the optimum keys and high secured image data. These high secured data are stored in the block chain, ensur- ing the image security to be stored in edge nodes. The complete framework was experimented using Ethereum using Ganache API and Python3.19 are utilized as the major programs for designing the varied interfaces of the recommended model. The comprehensive experimentation is undertaken to assess the security strength of the recommended encryption scheme. The evaluation metrics like as NACI, UACI, Entropy and standard verification methods such as NIST standard tests are deployed and analyzed. To prove it security strength, proposed secured BC framework is compared with the wide-variety of secured frameworks. The experimental findings reveal that the suggested framework establishes a more robust and secure environment for image exchange, surpassing the performance of other blockchain-based systems in terms of integrity, robustness and security. Finally, the paper spreads the bright light of advantages in deploying the proposed framework to formulate the most secured envi- ronment in the IoT-Edge environment for medical image transmission.
